**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right binding Mortgage Logic.com. Targeted searches across the compensation mechanics (§ 5), Client covenants (§ 8), licence (§ 2) and confidentiality (§ 10) returned nothing responsive:

- **§ 5(a)** bills on a fixed schedule with monthly invoices — no usage-verification or true-up audit hook.
- **§ 6** runs in our favour: Client gets supporting documentation on request and a charge-contest right; there is no reciprocal TrueLink right to examine our books.
- **§ 8(f)** (anti-spam technical mechanisms within TrueLink's own Interface) and **§ 9** (Y2K repair access) are not usage audits.
- **§ 2(e)** gives Client access to usage statistics and log files — again a Client right.

Because no Vendor audit right exists, the position sits above the preferred checklist (no frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-allocation or system-access limits are needed where there is nothing to limit). Inserting audit machinery to "complete" the preferred elements would manufacture a Vendor right we do not currently face, so we have not proposed one. If TrueLink later seeks an audit right in negotiation, we would then require: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.
